title: Design Index
description: The living map of every design project and the artifacts that belong to it (PRDs, ticket briefs, design outputs, gap/verification/audit reports). Two jobs: (1) scope placement — before a new brief becomes a new design, it is compared against every project here to catch work that really belongs to an existing design (see scope-overlap-report.schema.json); (2) change propagation — artifacts declare what they depend on, so when one changes, everything downstream is flagged for review instead of silently drifting.

navigation.description: The product's navigation map: every link between surfaces, so a new design can see how it connects and what already links where. Updated in generation Step 12 from each design's user flow.

from.description: A surface, or an external source like 'email'.

label.description: What the user sees or taps.

projectId.description: The design that added the link.

id.description: Stable project ID — usually the originating ticket or PRD key, e.g. 'DES-512'.

status.description: Extending an 'approved' or 'shipped' project means a new revision of it, not a silent edit. 'deprecated' projects are still compared against (to catch reintroducing retired work) but are never recommended as a merge target.

scopeSummary.description: One or two sentences: what problem this design owns.

scopeTerms.description: Normalized domain terms this project owns, lowercase, singular — e.g. ['kpi', 'trend', 'date-range filter']. Compared by Jaccard overlap in the scope check, so keep them specific; generic words ('page', 'user', 'button') dilute the signal.

surfaces.description: Screens/areas of the product this project changes, e.g. ['dashboard', 'dashboard/toolbar']. Two projects editing the same surface is the strongest sign of overlap.

codePaths.description: Globs for the code that implements this design, e.g. 'src/app/dashboard/**'. This is how design context reaches development: when someone edits a file under these paths, tools/design_context.py shows this project's decisions, components and open review flags. Required once status is approved or shipped.

priorities.description: Copied from the project's ticket brief so new briefs can be compared priority-by-priority.

componentsUsed.description: Component/variant names this project uses, e.g. 'Button/icon-only'. Lets a related project reuse the same pieces rather than re-deciding them.

relatedProjects.description: Explicit cross-project relationships, recorded when a scope check routes work between projects.

relation.description: 'shares-pattern' = separate projects that must stay consistent on a shared interaction (e.g. the same date-range filter). 'links-to' / 'linked-from' = one design is an entry point into the other, so a change to either can break the flow.

artifacts.description: Every artifact belonging to this project, with its dependencies. This is the integration graph.

id.description: The artifact's own ID, e.g. 'DES-512-gap-1' or 'audit-report-DES-512-rev1'.

version.description: Bump on every change. A dependent's dependsOn[].version records which version it was built against.
The upstream version this artifact was built from. If the upstream's current version is higher, this artifact is stale.

reviewStatus.description: 'needs-review' = an upstream artifact changed after this one was built. Set automatically on propagation; only a human or a fresh re-run clears it.

reviewReason.description: Required when needs-review: which upstream changed and what changed in it.
